title: MM2H Silver Tier in 2026: What You Need and What It Really Costs
desc: The Silver tier is the entry point to Malaysia's federal MM2H programme. Here is what it asks for, what you actually pay, and the property side buyers often miss.
sections: Who the Silver tier is for

The Silver tier is the lowest of the three federal MM2H tiers. It suits retirees, remote earners with income from abroad, and families who want a long-stay base in Malaysia without committing the larger sums that Gold and Platinum need. It does not allow you to take a job in Malaysia, so it works best for people whose income comes from outside the country.
What you need to qualify

Since the programme was restructured in 2024, Silver applicants need a fixed deposit of USD 150,000 in a licensed Malaysian bank and a residential property purchase of at least RM600,000. The main applicant must be 25 or older. The pass runs for 5 years and can be renewed, and a spouse and children can usually be included under the same application. Applications go through a licensed MM2H agent approved by the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC).
The costs on top of the deposit

The deposit is your own money and stays in your name, but it is not the only cost. Budget for the participation fee and visa fees for each family member, the agent's service fee, and the costs of buying a home: stamp duty, which is higher for foreign buyers, legal fees and loan costs if you borrow. Fee schedules have changed more than once, so ask your agent for the current list before you transfer anything.
The property side most people miss

RM600,000 is the MM2H minimum, but each state also sets its own minimum price for foreign buyers, and in many popular areas that limit is higher. Foreign purchases also need state consent, which adds time. The MM2H property is generally expected to be held for around 10 years, so pick a home you are happy to keep, or one that rents well while you are away.
take: For most of my clients the Silver tier is the sensible starting point: the deposit is manageable and RM600,000 to RM1 million buys a good condo in Kuala Lumpur, Penang or Johor Bahru. The mistake I see is choosing the home last. Check the foreign buyer limit for your area first, then shortlist homes that meet both limits and that you would happily hold for ten years.
sources: iProperty: MM2H how to apply and FAQ

title: MM2H vs Thailand Privilege Visa: What You Pay and What You Get Back
desc: Thailand's Privilege visa is a fee you spend; MM2H is mostly money you keep. A side-by-side look at the real cost of a long stay in each country.
sections: Two very different models

Thailand Privilege, formerly called Thailand Elite, is a membership. You pay a one-off fee and get a long-stay visa plus perks such as airport service. Malaysia's MM2H works the other way round: most of the money you put in is a fixed deposit and a property that you still own. That single difference changes how the two compare.
What Thailand charges

Thailand Privilege fees are paid once for the whole period. Reports in 2026 list Gold at THB 900,000 for 5 years, Platinum at THB 1.5 million for 10 years, Diamond at THB 2.5 million for 15 years, and the invitation-only Reserve at THB 5 million for 20 years. The cheaper Bronze tier closed to new applicants at the end of September 2026. Adding a family member costs extra on the higher tiers. The fee is not refunded when the membership ends.
What MM2H asks for

MM2H's federal tiers ask for a fixed deposit of USD 150,000, USD 500,000 or USD 1 million, and a home of at least RM600,000, RM1 million or RM2 million, for a pass of 5, 15 or 20 years. The deposit stays in your name and earns interest, and the home is an asset you can live in, rent out and eventually sell. The true cost is the fees, the buying costs and what the money could have earned elsewhere.
Which one costs less

If you only want a visa and plan to rent, Thailand's entry tier needs far less cash up front. If you want to own a home in the country anyway, MM2H can work out cheaper over time, because the money goes into a deposit and a property rather than a fee. Neither programme gives a path to citizenship, and work is only allowed on MM2H's Platinum tier.
take: Clients who compare the two often look only at the entry price. I ask them a different question: do you want to own a home here? If yes, MM2H turns most of your outlay into an asset, and Kuala Lumpur still offers more space per ringgit than Bangkok's prime areas. If you just want a few years of easy stays, Thailand's membership is simpler.
sources: The Thaiger: Thailand Privilege visa tiers, cost and benefits

title: MM2H Gold Tier: The Middle Route for Families Planning to Stay Long
desc: Gold gives a 15-year pass for a USD 500,000 deposit and a RM1 million home. Who it suits, and how it compares with Silver and Platinum.
sections: What Gold asks for

The Gold tier needs a fixed deposit of USD 500,000 in a licensed Malaysian bank and a residential property of at least RM1 million. In return you get a 15-year pass that can be renewed. The main applicant is generally expected to be 25 or older, and a spouse and children can usually be added to the same application.
Why families pick Gold

Fifteen years covers most of a child's schooling, which is why families often choose Gold over Silver. One application, renewed far less often, means less paperwork across the years when children move from primary school to university. The RM1 million property level also matches what many families want anyway: a three-bedroom home near an international school.
What it does not give you

Gold does not allow employment in Malaysia, and it is not a path to citizenship or permanent residence. If you plan to run a business here or take a job, only the Platinum tier allows that. You are also expected to spend a minimum number of days in Malaysia each year, so check the current rule when you apply.
Choosing the home

Because the property is generally held for around 10 years, the home should work for your family for a long time. Look at schools, commute and hospitals before the developer brand. In many states the foreign buyer minimum is also around RM1 million or higher, so Gold buyers often meet both limits with the same home.
take: Gold is the tier I discuss most with families from China, Japan and Korea. The deposit is significant, but the 15-year pass removes the worry of frequent renewals. My advice is to choose the school first, then the home within 20 minutes of it.
sources: iProperty: MM2H how to apply and FAQ

title: MM2H Platinum Tier: The Only Route That Lets You Work and Invest
desc: Platinum asks for USD 1 million and a RM2 million home, and gives a 20-year pass with the right to work and run a business. When the premium makes sense.
sections: The highest federal tier

Platinum needs a fixed deposit of USD 1 million and a residential property of at least RM2 million. It gives the longest pass, 20 years, and it is renewable. Like the other tiers, the application goes through a licensed MM2H agent and includes your spouse and children.
The real difference: work rights

Platinum is the only MM2H tier that allows you to work, invest and run a business in Malaysia. For entrepreneurs who want to base a regional company in Kuala Lumpur, that single right can matter more than the extra deposit. Silver and Gold holders can live here but cannot take up employment.
What RM2 million buys

At RM2 million you are looking at large units in KL City Centre, TRX, Bangsar or Damansara Heights, or landed homes in established Selangor suburbs. Foreign buyer limits are usually met at this level. The property is generally held for around 10 years, so think about rental demand as well as your own use.
Is it worth it?

If you do not need work rights, Gold gives a long pass for half the deposit. Platinum makes sense when you will run a business here, when the 20-year horizon matters, or when you were going to buy a home above RM2 million anyway.
take: Most Platinum clients I meet are business owners moving a regional office or a family office to Kuala Lumpur. For them the work right is the point. If that is not you, put the difference into a better home under the Gold tier.
sources: iProperty: MM2H how to apply and FAQ

title: Forest City SFZ: Johor's Lower-Cost MM2H Route Near Singapore
desc: The Forest City Special Financial Zone has its own MM2H tier with a much smaller deposit. What it asks for, and the property catch.
sections: A separate MM2H tier

Forest City in Johor is a Special Financial Zone with its own MM2H route. Reports in 2026 describe a fixed deposit of USD 65,000 for applicants aged 21 to 49, or USD 32,000 for those 50 and above, with a 10-year renewable pass and a minimum annual stay of about 90 days.
The property condition

The catch is the property: it must be a Forest City residential home bought from the developer, generally from RM500,000, and it cannot be bought from a third party. Resale is restricted, and reports say the home generally has to be kept for 10 years. You do not have to live in it, but your money is tied to one development.
Who it suits

The route suits people who want the lowest entry into MM2H and like the idea of living close to Singapore. Younger applicants also benefit, since the minimum age is 21 rather than 25. The Johor-Singapore links, including the RTS Link to Woodlands, add to the appeal for people who work across the border.
Questions to ask first

Ask how rental demand and resale values in Forest City have moved, what the maintenance fees are, and how far daily needs such as schools and hospitals are. Compare it with a federal Silver tier home in Johor Bahru city, which costs more up front but gives you a wider choice of homes.
take: I tell clients to treat Forest City as two decisions: an MM2H route and a property purchase. The visa terms are attractive. The property needs the same care as any other: visit, check occupancy and rents, and only commit if you would be happy owning that home for ten years.
sources: Malay Mail: Forest City issues guidance on SFZ MM2H requirements

title: Sarawak S-MM2H: How Sarawak's Own Programme Differs
desc: Sarawak runs its own MM2H with a ringgit deposit, a higher minimum age and a short annual stay. The main terms and who it fits.
sections: A state-run programme

Sarawak manages its own version of MM2H, called S-MM2H, separately from the federal programme. Since January 2025 the main applicant needs a fixed deposit of RM500,000 with a bank in Sarawak, up from RM150,000 before. The main applicant must be at least 30.
Lighter stay rule

S-MM2H asks for at least 30 days a year in Sarawak, fewer than the federal tiers. Part of the deposit can be used later, with a minimum balance kept in the account, which helps people who want to buy a home in Kuching.
Life in Kuching

Kuching is quieter and cheaper than Kuala Lumpur, with good private hospitals and a relaxed pace. It suits retirees and nature lovers more than people who need a big-city job market or many international schools.
Things to check

Because the programme is run by the state, its rules can change on a different timetable from the federal tiers. Check the current deposit, fees and stay rule on the Sarawak government's official page before you apply.
take: S-MM2H is a good fit for retirees who want a calm life and lower costs. Most of my buyers still choose the federal tiers because they want Kuala Lumpur, Penang or Johor Bahru, but for the right person Kuching is a lovely base.
sources: The Sun: Sarawak's new S-MM2H requirements

title: Your MM2H Fixed Deposit: Where It Sits and What You Can Use It For
desc: The deposit is the biggest number in MM2H, but it stays your money. How it works, what it earns and the rules on using part of it.
sections: Your money, in your name

The MM2H fixed deposit is placed in your own name at a licensed Malaysian bank. It is not a fee. It earns interest like any fixed deposit, and it is returned when you leave the programme, subject to the bank's and the programme's terms.
Using part of it

The programme has allowed part of the deposit to be withdrawn for approved uses, such as buying the qualifying home, education or medical costs, while a minimum balance stays in place. The exact share and timing have changed over the years, so confirm the current rule with your MM2H agent before planning around it.
Currency and interest

Many applicants place the deposit in US dollars or convert it to ringgit. Each has a currency risk. Compare the rates offered by the panel banks, and think about which currency your future spending in Malaysia will be in.
Plan the cash flow
You need the deposit and the property money at roughly the same time. Map out when the deposit is placed, when the booking fee and down payment are due, and whether you will take a home loan.
take: Clients often worry that the deposit is locked away. In practice it is one of the safest parts of the plan. The part that needs more thought is timing: line up the deposit, the purchase and any loan so you are not paying for everything in the same month.
sources: iProperty: MM2H how to apply and FAQ

title: Budgeting for MM2H: Every Cost Beyond the Deposit
desc: The deposit and the home are the headline. Fees, stamp duty, legal costs and running costs add up. A checklist so nothing surprises you.
sections: Programme fees

Expect a participation fee for the main applicant, visa or pass fees for each family member, and the agent's service fee. Amounts differ by tier and have changed over time, so ask for the current schedule in writing before you start.
Buying costs

Foreign buyers pay a higher stamp duty rate on the purchase: reports say it rose to 8% from January 2026. Add legal fees for the sale and purchase agreement, state consent fees for foreign purchases, and loan costs if you borrow. Use the calculator on this site to estimate the total.
Running costs
After you buy, budget for maintenance fees and sinking fund, quit rent and assessment tax, insurance, and furnishing. If you rent the home out while away, add agency and management fees.
Living costs
Health insurance is usually required for MM2H. School fees are the biggest line for most families: international school fees in Kuala Lumpur vary widely, so shortlist schools early.
take: The families who are happiest with MM2H are the ones who budgeted for year one properly. Write down the deposit, the home, the stamp duty and fees, and six months of living costs. If that total feels comfortable, you are ready.
sources: iProperty: MM2H how to apply and FAQ
PropertyGuru: Malaysia foreign property rules and costs

title: MM2H and Property: Two Minimum Prices You Must Meet
desc: Your home must meet the MM2H tier minimum and your state's foreign buyer minimum. Why the second one often decides what you can buy.
sections: The MM2H minimum

Each federal tier sets a minimum purchase price: RM600,000 for Silver, RM1 million for Gold and RM2 million for Platinum. The home must be residential, and it is generally expected to be held for around 10 years.
The state minimum

Separately, every state sets the lowest price at which a foreigner may buy. Kuala Lumpur's is commonly cited as RM1 million. Other states set their own levels, and some differ by property type or district, so the figure for your exact area matters.
Why it matters for Silver

A Silver applicant may qualify for MM2H with a RM600,000 home, but if the state minimum in that area is RM1 million, the home still cannot be bought. In practice the higher of the two limits is your real starting price.
State consent and timing
Foreign purchases also need state consent, which adds weeks to the process. Developers and lawyers who handle foreign buyers regularly know the steps.
take: This is the most common surprise for my MM2H clients. Before we look at any project, I check the foreign buyer limit for the area, then shortlist only homes that clear both numbers. It saves a lot of disappointment.
sources: PropertyGuru: Malaysia foreign property rules and costs

title: How an MM2H Application Works, Step by Step
desc: From choosing a tier to the pass in your passport: the order of steps, who does what, and where the property purchase fits in.
sections: 1. Choose your tier and area

Decide between Silver, Gold, Platinum or a state programme based on your budget, family and whether you need to work. Choose the city at the same time, because schools and property prices differ a lot between Kuala Lumpur, Penang and Johor Bahru.
2. Apply through a licensed agent

Applications go through an MM2H agent licensed by the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC). The agent prepares your documents, which usually include passports, proof of funds, health checks and police clearance.
3. Approval, deposit and home

After conditional approval, you place the fixed deposit and buy the qualifying home within the time allowed. This is where a property agent who knows MM2H and foreign buyer rules helps: the timing between approval, booking and the sale and purchase agreement matters.
4. Pass endorsement
Once the conditions are met, the MM2H pass is endorsed in your passport and your family's. Keep records of the deposit and property, as they are checked at renewal.
take: My part starts at step 3, but I like to meet clients at step 1. When the home is chosen alongside the tier, the purchase can be ready the moment approval comes through, and nobody rushes a decision on a home they will keep for ten years.
sources: iProperty: MM2H how to apply and FAQ

title: Bringing Your Family on MM2H: Spouse, Children and Parents
desc: One MM2H application can cover your spouse and children. What to know about dependants, schooling and bringing parents.
sections: Who can be included

A spouse and unmarried children can usually be included as dependants under the main applicant's MM2H pass. Rules on the maximum age of children and on including parents have changed over time, so check the current list with your agent.
Schooling

Children on MM2H generally attend international or private schools. Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Penang and Johor Bahru all have a wide choice, from British and American curricula to IB. Fees vary widely, and popular schools have waiting lists.
Healthcare
Malaysia's private hospitals are a major reason families choose MM2H. Health insurance is usually required for each family member, and older parents may face higher premiums.
Choosing the home for a family
Families do best near the school they choose, with a sensible commute and space to grow. Three bedrooms is a common minimum, and low-density developments with good facilities suit children well.
take: For families I always start with the school list, then draw a circle around it. The right home is usually within 15 to 20 minutes of school, which in Kuala Lumpur often points to Mont Kiara, Bangsar, Damansara Heights or Bukit Jalil.
sources: iProperty: MM2H how to apply and FAQ

title: MM2H vs Thailand LTR Visa: Assets, Income and Who Each One Suits
desc: Thailand's Long-Term Resident visa is built around wealth or income tests rather than a deposit and a home. How it compares with MM2H.
sections: Different tests

Thailand's LTR visa offers a 10-year stay to people who pass wealth, income or professional tests. The Wealthy Global Citizen track is commonly described as needing about USD 1 million in assets, with part invested in Thailand. Other tracks are based on pension or work income.
What MM2H asks instead
MM2H does not test your income in the same way. It asks for a fixed deposit and a home purchase in Malaysia. For people with savings but modest ongoing income, MM2H can be easier to qualify for.
Costs

The LTR's government fee is reported at around THB 50,000 per person, low compared with Thailand's Privilege membership. But the asset or income bar is high. MM2H's money mostly stays yours as a deposit and a property.
Which fits you

High earners and well-paid remote workers may find the LTR attractive. Families who want to own a home and settle long term may prefer MM2H. Both have changed their rules recently, so check the current criteria.
take: When clients compare the two, I ask what they want to own. The LTR is a visa; MM2H is a visa plus a home in your name. For families planning to stay ten years or more, owning the home usually wins.
sources: The Thaiger: Thailand LTR visa requirements

title: MM2H vs Singapore: Why Many Singapore Families Look at Johor
desc: Singapore has no retirement visa, and its investor route starts at S$10 million. Why MM2H in Johor or Kuala Lumpur is a common alternative.
sections: Singapore's options

Singapore does not offer a retirement visa. Its Global Investor Programme, which leads to permanent residence, is reported to start at S$10 million invested in a business, with higher amounts for fund and family office routes, and it is aimed at established business owners.
MM2H by comparison
MM2H asks for far less: from USD 150,000 in deposit and a RM600,000 home for Silver. It does not give permanent residence, but it gives a long, renewable stay.
The Johor angle
For people who work in or visit Singapore often, Johor Bahru offers MM2H with Singapore on the doorstep. The RTS Link and the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone add to the appeal.
Cost of living
Housing in Johor Bahru and Kuala Lumpur costs a fraction of Singapore's for the same space, and private healthcare and international schools are widely available.
take: Many of my Singapore-linked clients want space and a home they own, with Singapore within reach. MM2H in Johor Bahru or Kuala Lumpur gives them that for a sensible budget.
sources: Fragomen: Singapore Global Investor Program threshold increased

title: MM2H vs Portugal Golden Visa: Owning a Home vs Investing in a Fund
desc: Portugal removed property from its golden visa in 2023. How the two programmes now differ for people who want to own a home.
sections: Portugal dropped property

Portugal's golden visa used to be popular with property buyers, but the real estate routes were removed in October 2023. Today the main routes include investment funds, often cited at EUR 500,000, plus job creation, research and cultural contributions. Rules changed again in 2026, so check current amounts.
MM2H still includes a home
Malaysia's MM2H still links the visa to a property purchase. For buyers who want a home they can live in and rent out, that is now a clear difference.
Path to citizenship

Portugal's golden visa has been valued as a route to EU residence and later citizenship, though the residence period for citizenship is being lengthened. MM2H gives no citizenship path; it is a long-stay programme.
Lifestyle and cost
Kuala Lumpur and Penang offer lower living costs, a large English-speaking community and strong private healthcare. Portugal offers EU access and a European lifestyle.
take: Clients choosing between the two usually want different things. If an EU passport is the goal, Portugal is the conversation. If you want a home in a warm, affordable Asian city with your money in assets you control, MM2H fits better.
sources: Global Citizen Solutions: Portugal golden visa changes

title: MM2H vs UAE Golden Visa: Two Property-Linked Routes Compared
desc: Both link a long-stay visa to property. The UAE asks for AED 2 million in property for 10 years; MM2H asks for a deposit plus a home.
sections: The UAE property route

The UAE's 10-year Golden Visa can be obtained through property worth at least AED 2 million. Rules on mortgaged and off-plan property have been changing, so buyers should confirm the current position with the Dubai Land Department.
How MM2H differs
MM2H combines a fixed deposit with a home, at lower property levels: from RM600,000 for Silver. The total entry cost for Silver is well below the UAE's property threshold.
Tax and living

The UAE has no personal income tax, which draws many high earners. Malaysia taxes income earned in Malaysia; how foreign income is treated has changed in recent years, so take tax advice for your own case.
Lifestyle
Dubai offers a fast-paced, international city in the Gulf. Kuala Lumpur and Penang offer greener cities, lower living costs and easy access to the rest of Southeast Asia.
take: Clients who compare Dubai and Kuala Lumpur often like both. The choice usually comes down to tax and lifestyle. On property, your ringgit goes much further here: RM1 million to RM2 million buys a large, well-located home.
sources: Bayut: Real estate investor visas in the UAE

title: MM2H vs Indonesia Second Home Visa: Bali Dreams vs Owning a Home
desc: Indonesia's Second Home Visa asks for about IDR 2 billion in funds. How it compares with MM2H, especially on owning property.
sections: Indonesia's offer

Indonesia's Second Home Visa offers a 5 or 10-year stay to people who can show about IDR 2 billion, roughly USD 130,000, in an Indonesian bank or in qualifying assets. It is popular with people drawn to Bali.
Owning property

Foreigners face tight limits on owning land in Indonesia, and many villa deals are leaseholds or held through structures. In Malaysia, foreigners can own strata and landed title directly, subject to state minimums and consent.
Deposit compared
The Indonesian fund requirement is similar in size to MM2H Silver's USD 150,000 deposit. The difference is what else you get: MM2H links the stay to a home you own.
Infrastructure
Kuala Lumpur and Penang offer big-city healthcare, rail and international schools. Bali offers a resort lifestyle with fewer of those services.
take: Bali is a wonderful holiday. For a long-term base where you own your home outright and have city-level healthcare and schools, Malaysia is usually the stronger choice.
sources: ASEAN Briefing: Indonesia's second home visa requirements

title: MM2H vs Philippines SRRV: Comparing Two Retirement-Style Visas
desc: The SRRV asks for a smaller deposit and suits retirees. How it compares with MM2H on cost, eligibility and owning a home.
sections: What the SRRV asks

The Philippines' Special Resident Retiree's Visa was restructured in 2025. Reports say the minimum age fell to 40 and deposits start from about USD 15,000 for pensioners aged 50 and above, rising for younger or non-pensioner applicants.
Lower entry, different scope
The SRRV costs far less to enter than MM2H. But MM2H's property link and city infrastructure appeal to families and buyers who want a long-term home in a well-connected city.
Owning a home
In the Philippines foreigners can generally own condominium units but not land. In Malaysia foreigners can buy both strata and landed homes, subject to state rules.
Who chooses which
Retirees on a tight budget often look at the SRRV. Families and buyers who want a home in a major city with strong private healthcare often choose MM2H.
take: When budget is the only factor, the SRRV wins on entry cost. When clients add schools, healthcare and owning a home they can rent out, Kuala Lumpur and Penang usually come out ahead.
sources: ACCRA Law: Updates on the Philippines' retirement visa program

title: MM2H vs Japan: Why Japanese Retirees and Families Look at Malaysia
desc: Japan has no retirement visa, and its business manager visa got much stricter in 2025. Why Malaysia is a popular long-stay base for Japanese.
sections: For foreigners moving to Japan

Japan does not offer a retirement visa. The business manager visa, once a common route, became much stricter in October 2025: reports say the capital requirement rose from JPY 5 million to JPY 30 million, with a full-time employee and other conditions added.
For Japanese moving abroad

Malaysia has long been a favourite long-stay destination for Japanese retirees, thanks to a warm climate, lower costs, good private hospitals and established Japanese communities in Kuala Lumpur and Penang.
MM2H for Japanese families
MM2H gives a long, renewable stay with a home you own. Japanese schools and Japanese-speaking clinics in Kuala Lumpur make the move easier for families.
Practical points
Think about health insurance, pension payments abroad and tax. Talk to a tax adviser in both countries before you move.
take: Japanese clients often tell me they want the convenience of Japan with lower costs and more space. Areas like Mont Kiara and Bangsar, with Japanese supermarkets and schools nearby, are where they usually feel at home.
sources: KPMG: Japan business manager visa changes

title: MM2H vs Australia: After the Investor Visas Closed
desc: Australia closed its investor visa streams in 2024. What that means for people who want a long-term base, and why MM2H is still open.
sections: Australia's change

Australia's Business Innovation and Investment Program, including the Significant Investor stream, closed to new applicants in July 2024. As of 2026, no direct replacement for investor-based visas has been announced.
What remains
Australia's remaining routes focus on skills, employer sponsorship and exceptional talent. There is no longer a simple way to buy residence through investment.
MM2H stays open
Malaysia's MM2H continues to accept applications, with clear financial requirements. For people who want a long-term base in the region, it remains one of the most accessible options.
Being close to Australia
Kuala Lumpur is a short flight from Perth and other Australian cities. Some families keep ties in Australia while living in Malaysia for lower costs.
take: With Australia's investor doors closed, I meet more families who want a base in the region that they can actually qualify for. MM2H gives them a long stay and a home they own, a few hours from Australia.
sources: Widen: Business visa Australia 2026 after the BIIP closure

title: MM2H vs Greece Golden Visa: Two Property Routes, Different Price Tags
desc: Greece raised its golden visa property levels to EUR 400,000 and EUR 800,000. How that compares with MM2H's property minimums.
sections: Greece's new levels

Greece raised its golden visa property thresholds: reports describe EUR 800,000 in high-demand areas such as Athens, Thessaloniki, Mykonos and Santorini, and EUR 400,000 elsewhere, generally for a single property of at least 120 square metres. A lower level applies to certain conversion or restoration projects.
Price compared
At EUR 400,000 or more, Greece's entry is several times MM2H Silver's RM600,000 property minimum, even after adding the MM2H deposit.
What each gives
Greece gives EU residence and Schengen travel. MM2H gives a long-stay pass in Malaysia, without EU access but at a much lower total cost.
Lifestyle
Greece offers Mediterranean life in Europe. Malaysia offers modern cities, lower costs and easy travel across Asia.
take: If EU residence is the priority, Greece is worth a look. If you want a comfortable home in a growing Asian city for a fraction of the cost, MM2H gives far more space for the money.
